claim: In the matching retail DLL, the two compiler-generated iterator types returned by FACT-0115 each expose the same four exact IEnumerator support shapes. For <CoChange_BGMandPlay>c__Iterator8, tokens 0x060074EB and 0x060074EC are seven-byte Current getters that return field $current (0x0400C242); Dispose (0x060074ED) is a 15-byte body that writes $disposing=true (0x0400C243) then $PC=-1 (0x0400C244); Reset (0x060074EE) is a six-byte body that constructs System.NotSupportedException through MemberRef 0x0A0000EE and throws it. For <CoChange_BGMandPlay_FromAssetBundle>c__Iterator9, tokens 0x060074F1 and 0x060074F2 return $current (0x0400C24A); Dispose (0x060074F3) writes $disposing=true (0x0400C24B) then $PC=-1 (0x0400C24C); Reset (0x060074F4) has the same six-byte NotSupportedException throw body. FACT-0115 pins the exact generated iterator TypeDefs to which these methods belong.
